description: From the official viewpoint, the Corta Atalaya opens as a vast terraced bowl — once among the largest open pits in the world at 1,200 m long and 350 m deep — its mineral walls banded in rust-red, ochre and violet under moonlight. The dark depths far below hold the pit's stillness, the famous red Rio Tinto flowing somewhere beyond the rim. On a clear 21°C night with almost no wind, the moonscape of Europe's largest open-pit mine feels like another planet.
